title: Portfolio quote auto-refresh has no overlap guard or request cancellation, causing an unbounded in-flight backlog once any symbol resolves slowly
repro: Open the Portfolio panel with holdings that include a symbol not covered by fast providers (e.g. small/delisted NSE tickers that only nse_direct attempts, each call ~0.3-1.6s per fallthrough). QUOTE_REFRESH_MS=5000 fires setInterval(() => setQuotesNonce(n=>n+1), 5000) with no in-flight check; the fetch effect's `cancelled` flag only gates the .then()/.catch() state write, it never aborts the underlying fetch (no AbortController/signal anywhere in api.ts). Every 5s tick starts a brand-new full Promise.all fan-out on top of whatever is still in flight. Verified live: seeded my sidecar with a 100-holding portfolio including ~9 symbols with no EOD data (ABAN, ABINFRA, ABMINTLLTD, ACCURACY, ACSTECH, 3IINFOLTD, AARNAV, AARTECH, AARTISURF); the sidecar log shows an unbroken, non-decreasing cycle through the exact same 9 symbols for 4.5+ minutes (05:45:07 through past 05:50) with zero progress, continuing even after the originating test client process had fully exited (confirmed via ps aux / lsof -i :52324 -sTCP:ESTABLISHED showing no established connections at 05:50). A direct 20-symbol concurrent curl probe against my sidecar timed out at 60s; the identical RELIANCE.NS quote query against the separate, unrelated shared :52152 stack (same candidate code, no backlog) answered in 8ms, proving the hang is instance-specific accumulated backlog, not a systemic code defect in the provider itself. The sidecar self-recovered after the backlog eventually drained (~10 additional minutes idle, confirmed via a background watch probe: relianceQuote http=200 took=0s, RECOVERED) -- so this is a resource-exhaustion / temporary-DoS bug, not a permanent hang, but during the backlog window the panel's live quotes are completely unusable and the sidecar's worker pool is saturated by redundant retries of calls that were already known-unresolvable seconds earlier.

title: Agent fabricates SIFY's ADR ratio as 1:1 (true ratio is 1 ADS = 6 ordinary shares) with a fake 'fundamentals data' citation, on top of restating the same currency-mislabeled $46.5B revenue figure
repro: vy invoke, provider openrouter model nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free, autonomy=ask, prompt "How many ordinary shares does one SIFY ADR represent, and what is SIFY's TTM revenue in USD?" -> tool_use resolve_symbol, fundamentals, financial_statements -> final text: "SIFY's ADR is a 1:1 ratio—each SIFY ADR represents one ordinary share of Sify Technologies Limited. The company's trailing twelve-month (TTM) revenue is $46.51 billion USD (₹46,506,049,536). [Source: fundamentals data for SIFY]". Ground truth (battery pack P17_SIFY.json, face_value/shareholding notes, SEC 20-F-sourced): 1 ADS = 6 ordinary equity shares, a designated 'hostile trait' trap for this symbol precisely because getting the ratio wrong silently produces 6x-off per-share math. None of the three tools called (resolve_symbol/fundamentals/financial_statements) plausibly returns an ADR-ratio field, so the 1:1 figure is fabricated and falsely attributed to 'fundamentals data'; the $46.51B revenue claim for a company whose real TTM revenue is ~$492M (per the same battery pack) is also stated as flat fact with no plausibility check, even though SIFY is independently known to be loss-making (TTM net loss -$9.65M) which is starkly inconsistent with $46.5B revenue. CROSS-MODEL CONFIRMED: the same prompt on llama3.1:8b/Ollama (docs/redesign/verification/r15/rc1/scenarios/ollama-sk4-sify.jsonl) independently produced "One SIFY ADR represents 1 ordinary share" / "The ADR for Sify Technologies represents 1 common share" — same wrong ratio, different model, no shared prompt-injection cause; this is not a single model's quirk.
suspected_files: sidecar/services/agent_tools (fundamentals/financial_statements handlers — no ADR-ratio field, no plausibility bound)
sidecar/agents/*.json (no instruction to refuse/hedge on data the tool result does not contain)

title: nse_direct's process-wide throttle serializes concurrent snapshot_structured legs past their shared 6s witness timeout
repro: In-process, candidate sidecar venv, PYTHONPATH=sidecar, VYSTED_DATA_DIR=<own seed copy>: `await asyncio.gather(agent_tools.invoke_tool('price_data', {'symbol': 'RELIANCE'}), agent_tools.invoke_tool('fundamentals', {'symbol': 'RELIANCE'}))` takes ~18.3s combined (both legs individually succeed in 1-3s when called alone, sequentially). Called through `services.research.fast.snapshot_structured(..., 'RELIANCE', region='IN')`, both legs report `{'ok': False, 'error': '... timed out after 6s — dropped'}` even though the underlying data is available and each fetch alone is fast. Root cause: services/nse_provider.py's module-level `_Throttle` (min_interval=1.0s+jitter) and `_lock` (threading.Lock around the actual session.get call) serialize ALL nse_direct HTTP calls process-wide (an intentional anti-bot pacer, tagged 'R15-DATA-066' in a comment, not new to batch-6). services/research/fast.py's `_WITNESS_LEG_TIMEOUT_S = 6.0` time-boxes price+fundamentals AND all 7 cross-check witness legs (dividend TTM, growth, ownership, declared dividend, earnings quality, 52-week range, market-cap witness) independently and concurrently via the same asyncio.gather fan-out — up to 9 concurrent tasks can all be waiting on the same serialized nse_direct resource at once, so later-queued legs routinely exceed the shared 6s budget purely from queueing, not from any real slowness or failure in the data itself.

title: DEEP brief's auto-generated 'web sources alone' coverage note is false when the up-front price/fundamentals snapshot times out but the research loop's own tool calls later populate structured sources
repro: Own sidecar 127.0.0.1:52321 (rc1-cand source, data dir scratchpad/rc1-data-rc1-drive-research-briefs). scripts/r15/vy.py invoke copilot 'Bharat Dynamics — order book, margins and valuation' --provider openai --model gpt-4o-mini --autonomy auto --options '{"research_depth":"deep"}' --port 52321. The up-front structured snapshot fails (structured.price.ok=false, structured.fundamentals.ok=false, both 'timed out after 6s — dropped'), which correctly satisfies sidecar/services/research/deep.py:structured_feeds_available()==False and appends the WEB_ONLY_FLOOR_NOTE ('no structured price or fundamentals feed covered this instrument ... the coverage for this brief comes from web sources alone'). But later in the same run the researcher's own fundamentals/price tool calls succeed and get recorded into findings.structured_sources (vysted://price/BDL, vysted://fundamentals/BDL both appear in the published sources[] list at indices 6-7), and the brief's own lead figures cite them directly: '**Stock Price**: ₹1155.0 ... [6]' and '**Market Capitalization**: ... [6]' where source [6] = vysted://price/BDL. The note and the citations directly contradict each other: the note tells the user the brief is 'web sources alone' while the headline numbers are demonstrably structured-provenance, not web-scraped.
